title: Bidirectional A*: Find the Fastest Route in Tallinn!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* search from both the start and goal on a real street graph, shrinking the explored area. The moment the two frontiers meet, the optimal path is reconstructed with A*’s informed efficiency.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ Tallinn (Kalamaja) streets, but turned into a graph! In this visualization, **Bidirectional A*** runs two coordinated A* searches: one forward from the start node and one backward from the destination node. 

🔍 Each frontier expands using a priority queue keyed by **f(n)=g(n)+h(n)**, where **g(n)** is the traveled cost and **h(n)** is a heuristic (typically straight-line distance on coordinates) to guide exploration. Because we grow from **both ends**, the algorithm often reduces the search space dramatically—then when the paths **meet at a common node**, we stitch the partial routes into the final shortest path. 

🗺️📍 Under the hood, real street maps become a **weighted graph** (intersections = nodes, road segments = edges), and pathfinding becomes a classic graph-search problem. 

👉 Want the shortest-path explanation for *your* city next? Drop a city/district in the comments and hit follow for more algorithm visualizations! 🚀
fb_caption:
🚦 Pathfinding on real maps, explained with **Bidirectional A***! We convert Tallinn’s streets into a weighted graph (nodes at intersections, edges as road segments), then run A* search **from both the start and goal at the same time**. 

When the two search frontiers meet, the algorithm reconstructs the optimal route efficiently—often exploring far less than a single-direction search. 📚
